verdicts.why: To try someone's patience is to strain or test it; any irritation lies in the situation, and the verb itself takes no side against the strainer or the strained, the same as 'test' would.
A technical cookery sense (render fat) that names a process and carries no attitude toward it.
Handing over money for goods or services is described plainly; the word neither approves nor sneers.
Discharging a debt is named neutrally; 'debt' is an unwelcome referent but the verb takes no side.
Bearing a cost or penalty for one's action is a plain statement of consequence; the penalty is the bad referent, not the word.
Paying attention or respects is a light-verb use that describes the act of giving and carries no attitude of its own.
Doing or giving something in return (paying a visit, a compliment) is descriptive; the word does not colour what is given.
Making compensation for damage or loss is stated without judgement of the payer or the wrong.
Saying a course of action pays states that it is profitable or worthwhile; that is the meaning, not an attitude beyond it.
An investment that pays a return is described in plain financial terms with no colouring.
As an intensifier ('a real superiority', 'real concern') it strengthens whatever the noun already says and adds no attitude of its own; a strong meaning is not a loaded word.
Something capable of being treated as fact is being classified, not judged.
Not imaginary versus imaginary is a distinction of substance, and the word carries no approval beyond that distinction.
Coinciding with reality is a descriptive property, not an evaluation of the thing that has it.
An economics term of art (real versus nominal) with no attitude attached.
A legal classification of property (real versus personal) that judges nothing.
A state of ease is a pleasant referent named plainly; the word does not itself signal the speaker's approval or contempt.
Living in comfort names a level of means without praising or sneering at those who have it.
A piece of bedding, named plainly.
The legal formula 'aid and comfort' names assistance to an enemy in neutral terms; the disapproval belongs to the referent, not the word.
Being a student of a subject is described without any attitude toward the learner or the subject.
Committing something to memory is a plain description of an act.
Using 'learn' for 'teach' marks the speaker's dialect or register rather than any attitude toward the person taught, so it does not judge its object.
The psychological sense (schema, a mental model) is a technical term with none of the cunning that the plan sense can carry.
A relativity-theory point in space-time is a technical term with no attitude.
